THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Weston wrapped up a nearly three-decade tax-increment financing district that added $354 million in assessed value, while Kronenwetter's village board moved forward on industrial rezoning and a new community fundraiser.

  • The Village of Weston's CDA voted unanimously to redeem its 2017A lease revenue bonds early, eliminating debt payments that had been scheduled through 2031 as TIF District No. 1 officially closes.
  • Weston staff are directed to bring the question of the CDA's future role — including potential disbandment — to the Village Board's next monthly meeting.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved rezoning Marathon County Highway Department property to M2 General Industrial, clearing the way for the county to proceed with facility development.
  • Kronenwetter's board approved a Bushka Park 5K/3K run/walk fundraiser for September 12, 2026, and matched a $5,000 parks grant; the Parks Committee will finalize event details.
  • The Wausau School Board's special meeting is set to consider approving the 2026-27 teacher salary schedule and updated employee handbook ahead of the new school year.
  • Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee is set to consider a temporary moratorium on data center development applications and a potential oak wilt ordinance at its Monday meeting.

Coming up: On Monday, the Wausau School Board holds a special meeting at 5:00 PM followed immediately by a workshop expected to cover school perceptions survey results and possible referendum considerations; also Monday, Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee meets at 6:00 PM to weigh the data center moratorium and oak wilt ordinance. Marathon County's Health & Human Services Committee meets Thursday at 5:00 PM.
